doc.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Road bands and the Gillespie band
title: Trenier Brothers, Lucky Millinder and New York jobs
summary: The first bands he left home with, with Lucky Thompson's help, then Hot Lips Page, Roy Eldridge and Ernie Fields.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Just to go back for a second, who were some of the groups that you were touring with before you returned to Detroit?

Okay um the first group I left home with was The Trenier Brothers Band. Uh Lucky Thompson was in that band, and Sonny Stitt was in that band. Lucky Thompson recommended me, uh and I joined them in Chicago around 1944. And the band only–we worked at the Ritz Theatre in Chicago. And it’s interesting, at that time, Sonny Stitt sounded in the vein of Carter...Benny Carter.

Um...but that was before any of us had heard Hootie Blues with Jay McShann and Charlie Parker, and Sonny made about-face and he seemed like more influenced by Charlie Parker. Um anyway, that band only lasted a couple of weeks, and so I returned to Detroit. And then in about ’46, Lucky Thompson recommended to the Lucky Millinder Band. So I joined them in New York in about ’46. Um, at least I, he sent for me. I went to New York, I was supposed to take the tenor player’s place who was supposed to go with Cab Calloway. Something happened, he didn’t go with Cab Calloway [laughing], as it was. And uh so he paid me for two weeks, as the union says you should do, and I stayed in New York. I didn’t want to return home. So during that period, I played with Hot Lips Page and Roy Eldridge uh...and I finally I left town with a territory band called Ernie Fields...
